title: FAR U1·W4 — Leases (ASC 842) & Contingencies (ASC 450) (CPA Core · from CMA m7/m10)
lessonHtml:
Cold open — the leased equipment is now on the balance sheet

CMA month 7 flagged that ASC 842 brought operating leases onto the balance sheet. FAR is where that is measured. MBG leases vehicles and equipment, and under ASC 842 a lessee recognizes a right-of-use (ROU) asset and a lease liability for essentially every lease over twelve months. This week measures leases and then covers loss contingencies — warranty, litigation, and bond-claim accruals.

Lessee accounting under ASC 842

At commencement, the lessee records a lease liability at the present value of the remaining lease payments, discounted at the rate implicit in the lease (or the incremental borrowing rate if that is not determinable), and an ROU asset equal to the liability plus initial direct costs and prepayments, less incentives. Both finance and operating leases are on the balance sheet; the difference is the expense pattern.

Worked measurement

Illustrative: five annual payments of $50,000 at an 8% discount rate. The ordinary-annuity present-value factor (8%, 5 years) is 3.9927, so the lease liability = $50,000 × 3.9927 = $199,635, and the ROU asset begins at the same amount (absent initial direct costs).

Finance versus operating classification

A lease is a finance lease (lessee) if any one criterion is met: ownership transfers at the end; a purchase option is reasonably certain to be exercised; the lease term is a major part of the asset's remaining life; the present value of payments is substantially all of the asset's fair value; or the asset is so specialized it has no alternative use to the lessor. Otherwise it is an operating lease.

The expense pattern differs: a finance lease records amortization of the ROU asset plus interest on the liability — front-loaded total expense. An operating lease records a single straight-line lease expense. Both reduce the same lease liability as payments are made.

Loss contingencies (ASC 450)

A loss contingency is accounted for by likelihood:

  • Probable and reasonably estimable → accrue a liability and recognize the loss (if a range, accrue the best estimate, or the minimum of the range when no amount is better).
  • Reasonably possible (or probable but not estimable) → disclose only.
  • Remote → generally ignore (no accrual, no disclosure).

For MBG, a probable, estimable warranty obligation or an adverse, estimable litigation outcome is accrued; a merely possible performance-bond claim is disclosed. Gain contingencies are not accrued (to avoid recognizing income before realization); they may be disclosed if probable.

CMA bridge

CMA month 7 (week 4) introduced ASC 842 at a conceptual level and month 10 covered risk; FAR measures the lease liability and ROU asset and sets the accrual rules for the warranty and litigation contingencies that risk management identifies. The threads connect: identify the risk in CMA, measure and disclose it in FAR.

Practice and recap

  1. Recognize an ROU asset and lease liability at the present value of lease payments for leases over twelve months.
  2. Classify finance vs operating by the five criteria; know the expense patterns differ.
  3. Accrue a loss contingency that is probable and estimable; disclose if reasonably possible; ignore if remote.
  4. Do not accrue gain contingencies.

Recap: ASC 842 puts the $199,635 lease liability and ROU asset on MBG's balance sheet; finance leases front-load expense while operating leases are straight-line; and loss contingencies are accrued only when probable and estimable, with gain contingencies never accrued.

flashcards.back: An ROU asset and a lease liability for essentially all leases over 12 months (finance and operating both on-balance-sheet).
Present value of remaining lease payments at the implicit rate (or incremental borrowing rate).
ROU amortization plus interest on the liability — front-loaded total expense.
Accrue a liability and recognize the loss.
No; they are not accrued (may be disclosed if probable).

questions.q: Under ASC 842, a lessee with a 5-year equipment lease recognizes:
choices: An ROU asset and a lease liability
Rent expense only, off balance sheet
questions.explain: ASC 842 puts both finance and operating leases on-balance-sheet as an ROU asset and lease liability.

questions.q: Five annual payments of $50,000, 8% annuity factor 3.9927. The initial lease liability is:
Which expense pattern belongs to an OPERATING lease (lessee)?
questions.explain: Operating leases record a single straight-line lease expense; finance leases front-load.

questions.q: Which condition makes a lease a FINANCE lease?
choices: The term is a small part of the asset's life
A purchase option is reasonably certain to be exercised
Payments are a small fraction of fair value
The asset has many alternative uses
questions.explain: A reasonably certain purchase option is one of the five finance-lease criteria.

questions.q: A loss contingency that is probable and reasonably estimable should be:
choices: Accrued as a liability with a loss
questions.explain: Probable and estimable loss contingencies are accrued and the loss recognized.

questions.q: A loss contingency that is only reasonably possible should be:
questions.explain: Reasonably possible contingencies are disclosed, not accrued.
Gain contingencies are not accrued to avoid recognizing income before realization; disclosure may be appropriate.
